reply:
❌ Not real — the claim is drastically overstated.

Cold plunges do boost metabolism briefly (thermogenesis during cold exposure), but "doubling it for 24 hours" is myth. The metabolic spike is temporary and modest — your body burns a bit extra while cold-adapted, then returns to baseline. The cold-catching claim also lacks solid evidence; some studies show modest immune shifts, but claiming a 50% risk cut is cherry-picking.

The real takeaway: cold plunges have minor metabolic and maybe immune effects, but they're not a health hack. Consistency, sleep, and movement matter way more.
description: Two-part claim where evidence supports one half and refutes the other — needs a nuanced verdict

expect.reply_should: A MIXED verdict distinguishing the halves: metabolism boost is real but transient (not 24h doubling); illness reduction exists (~29% sick days in one RCT) but 'cut in half' overstates. Blanket true/false fails.
